categories.main_business_segments: Avnet operates two primary business segments: Electronic Components (EC), which markets and distributes semiconductors, interconnect/passive/electromechanical components, and embedded solutions to high and medium-volume customers; and Farnell, which distributes electronic components, kits, tools, and test/measurement products to lower-volume customers primarily through e-commerce. EC represents 93.5% of sales while Farnell represents 6.5% of sales.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Avnet is primarily a distributor rather than a manufacturer. Core competencies include global warehousing and logistics, supply chain management, design chain support with engineering resources, embedded systems integration and assembly, and e-commerce platforms. The company leverages franchised distribution agreements with suppliers and provides value-added services including testing, assembly, programming, and supply chain optimization.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Avnet serves a diverse customer base including startups, mid-sized businesses, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), electronic manufacturing services (EMS) providers, and original design manufacturers (ODMs). Key end markets include industrial, automotive, aerospace and defense, telecommunications, medical, and digital editing sectors. Approximately 81% of sales are semiconductors, indicating heavy exposure to technology and industrial markets.
categories.geographic_coverage: Avnet operates globally across three major economic regions: Americas (25.7% of sales), Europe/Middle East/Africa (34.8% of sales), and Asia/Pacific (39.5% of sales). The company has operations in more than 140 countries with approximately 15,800 employees across 48 countries. Significant operations include facilities in the United States, Germany, Belgium, United Kingdom, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Singapore.
categories.supply_chain_position: Avnet operates in the midstream of the electronics supply chain as a distributor. The company purchases products from leading electronic component manufacturers and distributes them to OEMs, EMS providers, and other customers. Avnet also provides value-added services including supply chain solutions, logistics, inventory management, and design support, positioning it as an intermediary between suppliers and end customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding design chain and supply chain solutions, developing embedded and integrated solutions for specialized applications, enhancing e-commerce capabilities through the element14 online community, and investing in distribution center infrastructure. The company is investing in new distribution centers in EMEA to support future growth and implementing IT modernization initiatives including cloud environments and artificial intelligence applications.
categories.revenue_model: Avnet generates revenue primarily through product sales of electronic components and related products on a gross basis, recognizing revenue upon transfer of control to customers. The company also earns revenue from value-added services including design support, supply chain management, assembly, programming, and logistics services. Revenue is measured as consideration expected in exchange for transferring products, net of customer discounts and rebates.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Arrow Electronics, Future Electronics, World Peace Group, and WT Microelectronics for the EC segment; and Mouser Electronics, Digi-Key Electronics, and RS Components for Farnell. Avnet is one of the leading global electronic component distributors. Competitive advantages include breadth of supplier relationships, global footprint, value-added services, and ability to simplify customer procurement through a single source.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Avnet is a large-cap company with fiscal 2023 sales of $26.5 billion, up 9.2% from $24.3 billion in fiscal 2022. Net income was $770.8 million in fiscal 2023 compared to $692.4 million in fiscal 2022. The company has demonstrated consistent growth with three-year sales growth from $19.5 billion (fiscal 2021) to $26.5 billion (fiscal 2023). Operating income margin improved to 4.5% in fiscal 2023 from 3.9% in fiscal 2022.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Avnet differentiates through comprehensive design chain support with engineering resources and technical solutions, extensive supply chain optimization capabilities, broad supplier product line card enabling one-stop procurement, global distribution infrastructure with rapid delivery capabilities, and specialized value-added services tailored to customer needs. The company emphasizes helping customers accelerate time-to-market, optimize component selection, and manage supply chains efficiently without requiring significant capital investment.
